claims.text: Pre-coating tungsten particles with copper by atomic layer deposition before spark-plasma sintering will improve W–Cu interfacial bonding relative to vapor-coated W–Cu composites.
ALD pre-coating followed by spark-plasma sintering will reduce void formation relative to vapor-coated W–Cu composites.
Reduced void formation and improved interfacial bonding will produce superior thermal transport.
Reduced void formation and improved interfacial bonding will produce superior mechanical durability.
ALD can deposit a thin, uniform, conformal copper coating on tungsten surfaces.
Controlled ALD temperature and precursor exposure can ensure conformal copper coverage.
A spark-plasma-sintering temperature and time can be selected that melt copper without significant phase separation or void growth.
The ALD-derived W–Cu interface will promote densification during sintering.
The ALD-derived interface will promote uniform copper wetting along tungsten surfaces.
A pre-deposited copper layer enhances W–Cu wettability during rapid heating.
A pre-deposited copper layer enhances interfacial diffusion during rapid heating.
Enhanced wettability and interfacial diffusion reduce interfacial defects.
Voids and phase-separation sites impair thermal transport and durability in W–Cu composites.
The ALD-precoated composite will have higher effective thermal conductivity than a vapor-coated W–Cu composite.
The ALD-precoated composite will maintain or improve mechanical durability under fusion-joint service conditions relative to the baseline.
The ALD-precoated composite will have a more uniform microstructure and lower void fraction than the vapor-coated baseline.
Sintered vapor-coated tungsten powders can achieve near-perfect contact between W and Cu.
Vapor-coated W–Cu composites remain susceptible to void formation and microstructural inhomogeneity.
The proposed composite is intended to withstand sustained high heat flux and irradiation in fusion-reactor joints.

contradictions.description: The proposed comparison does not isolate the ALD intervention: the baseline uses vapor coating and conventional or standard sintering, while the test group uses ALD coating and spark-plasma sintering. This conflicts with the experimental statement that the groups differ only in the ALD step.
